spot.title: One token maintains the call exposure.
spot.caption: Product design: a spot asset representing a continuously rebalanced portfolio of fully paid calls.
spot.description: One Ethereum token represents a single-stock call strategy. The portfolio replaces contracts using its own assets; investors hold and trade the same token through successive rolls.

market.title: Two stocks already support billions in call premium.
market.caption: Snapshot: Schwab September 4 quotes; reported perpetual OI on September 7, 2026. Source notes define the measures and coverage.
market.description: Outstanding ATM/OTM premium value totals $8.05 billion: NVDA $3.63B and MU $4.42B. Their call underlying notionals are $84.99B and $57.30B, versus reported tracked perp OI of $359.3M and $428.3M. The two panels distinguish premium value from underlying notional.

basket.title: One stock. A basket of calls.
basket.caption: Illustrated basket based on the demonstrated five-call design. The rulebook defines allocation and residual cash.
basket.description: The demonstrated strategy selects five calls on one company in one expiration. Whole-contract sizing leaves residual cash. The rulebook defines the basket; actual holdings require execution.

roll.title: The contracts change. The investor keeps the token.
roll.caption: Roll timing follows the rulebook. Accounting amounts illustrate asset replacement and trading costs.
roll.description: Form the basket, retain or rebalance it, then replace it when the rule triggers. In the accounting example, $80 calls plus $20 cash become $85 replacement calls plus $15 cash; a $1 trading cost leaves $99.

products.title: Why the spot format is useful.
products.caption: The spot interface puts an options strategy inside the existing wallet and trading workflow.
products.description: Investors hold one maintained strategy. Wallets and exchanges integrate its ERC-20 shares. Liquidity providers trade the shares, and builders reuse the verification system for additional stocks.

payoff.title: Pay for convexity. Define the amount at risk.
payoff.caption: Illustrative single-call expiry payoff per underlying share, before fees. The tracker maintains a rolling basket of calls.
payoff.description: A $100-strike call bought for $10 has expiry profit max(stock price minus $100, zero) minus $10 per share. Maximum loss is $10; breakeven is $110; a $140 finish yields $30 profit. This plots payoff, without assigning outcome probabilities.

navcoin.title: One portfolio. Three responsibilities.
navcoin.caption: NAVCoin product architecture: brokerage assets, Post Fiat verification, and Ethereum ownership and markets.
navcoin.description: The broker holds calls and cash. In the full NAVCoin architecture, Post Fiat verifies accounting evidence and Ethereum enforces issuance and settlement authorizations. Investors hold portfolio shares and access a secondary market.

redemption.title: Two exits with different mechanics.
redemption.caption: A redeemable model offers market trading and primary settlement. Product terms determine timing and costs.
redemption.description: A Uniswap sale transfers existing tokens at the pool price. Primary redemption locks shares, values the claim, settles cash and reconciles assets and supply. Pending claims remain accounted for.

pipeline.title: Three jobs: collect, prove, record.
pipeline.caption: Measured collection binds the inputs. The proof checks the calculation. The ledger records the accepted result.
pipeline.description: Schwab inputs travel over TLS into a measured Nitro collector. SP1 checks attestation and input bindings, computes the target, and produces a proof. PFTL verifies and records the accepted receipt.

verification.title: Check the strategy you bought.
verification.caption: Interactive illustration of the registered-run acceptance checks.
verification.description: Interactive checks accept a matching registered run. Changed rules or inputs fail registration checks, altered target bytes fail proof verification, and a consumed run fails replay checks.

ledger.title: A shared record for every accepted target.
ledger.caption: The receipt lifecycle is implemented and locally qualified.
ledger.description: A registered run binds its program, method and inputs. Consensus verifies the submitted proof, records a receipt and supplies an accepted history for applications to query. This lifecycle is locally qualified.

status.title: The core calculation is proven. Build the funded product around it.
status.caption: September 6, 2026 demonstration; the linked record contains the effective parameters and qualification evidence.
status.description: September 6, 2026: MU and NVDA each produced five November 20 call targets. Attested inputs, real proofs, independent replay and local four-validator receipts passed. The funded product adds holdings, custody, NAV, issuance and settlement; the demo used hypothetical capital.
